base_member_text: [L3-L6,L10-L16,L51] (LOW/input-contract) The batch file dereferences positional arguments without presence checks and constructs the solution path with a forward slash, leaving invocation and path-format contracts implicit and fragile.
audit_member_text: [L10-L16] (LOW/argument-validation) Missing version arguments produce invalid unquoted IF comparisons rather than a controlled argument error.

base_member_text: [L8-L16,L21-L23] (MED/version/dispatch) The dispatcher recognizes VS2010/2012/2015/2017 but has no VS2008 label and no VS2019/VS2022 cases, so an unsupported or newer version falls through to the VS2008 toolchain while the repository contains newer solution files.
audit_member_text: [L10-L23,L51] (MED/unsupported-version-fallback) Unrecognized versions silently fall back to VS2008 while still constructing a solution name from that version, including the supplied newer IFX solutions.

[L21-L37,L59,L74] (HIGH/command-quoting) Older-version branches store quotes inside devenv_path and the invocation adds another pair, producing malformed executable quoting for paths containing spaces.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: L21-L37 include literal surrounding quotes in the older-version devenv_path values, and L59/L74 wrap the expansion in another pair without stripping them. This produces an executable token beginning with doubled quotes before a space-containing path; the unquoted VS2017 assignment does not neutralize the older branches.

adversarial.rationale: The VS2008/2010/2012/2015 branches assign literal quote characters with SET, whereas only VS2017 assigns an unquoted value (trunk/config/build_configuration.bat:21-44). Expansion at lines 59 and 74 therefore starts with two quotes before the space-containing executable path; the intervening code does not strip the stored quotes, and later ERRORLEVEL handling cannot repair the malformed invocation.
